title: Show Sticker or 3D Emblem Letters: Pick Size and Finish
meta_description: Choosing a show sticker in raised 3D letters? Five sizes from 8 to 16 letters, matte or mirror, from $39.95. Measure your space and pick in minutes.
body_html:
The right show sticker depends on three things: how many letters you need, how much flat space you have, and whether you want matte or mirror. Our 3D emblem comes in five sizes holding 8 to 16 letters, from $39.95.

On this page

  • How many letters fit at each size?
  • Which size fits the space you actually have?
  • Matte or mirror: which finish should you pick?
  • What will your show sticker cost?
  • Worked example: a nine-letter word on a short spot
  • What to confirm before you order

How many letters fit at each size?

Start here, because the letter count rules options out before you measure anything. Every size has a fixed letter limit, and a word that goes over it won't fit that size.

SizeMax lettersStarting priceSuits
2x4 inches8$39.95Short names, initials or one short word on a small spot, at the lowest price in the range.
2x6 inches12$59.95Most single names and mid-length words up to 12 letters.
2x8 inches16$79.95The longest text in the range: two short words or a long name, up to 16 letters.
3x8 inches12$79.95Up to 12 letters on a badge with a larger short side than 2x6 or 2x8.
4x8 inches8$79.95A short word of up to 8 letters on the largest badge in the range.

The table shows a trade-off. All three sizes with an 8-inch side start at $79.95, but their letter limits fall as the short side grows: 16 at 2x8, 12 at 3x8 and 8 at 4x8. So a bigger badge doesn't always hold more text. For a long word, 2x8 is the only size that goes past 12 letters.

How to apply it: write out your exact text and count every character, including spaces. Then cross off any row whose maximum is lower than your count. Counting spaces is the cautious choice. If your text only fits once spaces are left out, ask the shop how it counts them before you order.

What to check

  • Your full letter count, including any second word.
  • Whether your count lands right on a size's limit.
  • Which rows are left after the cross-off. Only those go on to the next step.

Which size fits the space you actually have?

Once you know which sizes can hold your word, the spot you're mounting it on decides between them. Each size is given as two numbers: 2x4, 2x6, 2x8, 3x8 and 4x8 inches. Three of the five have an 8-inch side, so a spot shorter than 8 inches on its long side leaves you with 2x4 or 2x6.

How to apply it: take a ruler or tape measure to the exact spot. Measure only the flat area, not the curve or edge around it, because a badge needs a surface it can sit flat against. Write down the long side and the short side. A size fits when your long side is at least its larger number and your short side is at least its smaller number. Go back to the rows you kept from the table and drop any size that fails either test.

If two sizes are still left, the choice comes down to presence. The larger badge fills more of the spot, and the smaller one leaves a margin around it. Neither is wrong. Cut masking tape to each size and stick it on the spot. You'll see which one looks right before you spend anything.

What to check

  • The flat long side and short side of the spot, in inches.
  • Whether the surface is flat across the whole area.
  • A tape mock-up of each size you're still choosing between.

Matte or mirror: which finish should you pick?

The emblem comes in two surfaces:

  • Matte Finishing: from $39.95
  • Mirror Finishing: from $49.95

Those are the lowest listed prices for each finish. They don't tell you what each finish costs at a given size, so check the live price once you've picked a size.

The practical difference is reflection. A mirror surface reflects whatever is around it, and a matte one doesn't. On a busy background, those reflections can make the letters look different depending on where you stand. On a plain surface, the same reflections are often what makes the letters stand out. Matte looks the same from any angle.

How to apply it: stand where people will usually see the sticker and look at what's behind the spot. A patterned or busy surface points toward matte. A plain, solid-colour surface gives mirror a clean backdrop.

You can switch between both surfaces and all five sizes to see how each finish looks on your size.

What to check

  • What surrounds the mounting spot, and how busy it is.
  • The live price for your size in each finish.
  • How each finish looks in the product photos at the size you picked.

What will your show sticker cost?

The full range runs from $39.95 to $89.95. These are the starting prices by size:

  • 2x4 inches: from $39.95
  • 2x6 inches: from $59.95
  • 2x8 inches: from $79.95
  • 3x8 inches: from $79.95
  • 4x8 inches: from $79.95

The top of the range, $89.95, is higher than every size's starting price. That means at some sizes, adding a finish or another option pushes the price above the starting figure. This page doesn't list the price for each size and finish pairing. The product page shows the exact figure as soon as you've picked both, so use that number, not the starting price, when you compare.

The useful pattern for a buyer is that the three sizes with an 8-inch side all start at the same price. If your word fits 2x8, 3x8 and 4x8, price won't decide between them. Your letter count and the short side of your spot will. The real price step sits between 2x6, at $59.95, and the 8-inch sizes, at $79.95.

How to apply it: take the sizes left over from the last two sections and set a ceiling. If 2x6 holds your word and fits the space, it costs less than any 8-inch size. Then pick each remaining size with your chosen finish on the product page, and write down the price it shows.

What to check

  • The starting price of each size still on your list.
  • The live price with your chosen finish added.
  • Shipping cost, shown at checkout.

Worked example: a nine-letter word on a short spot

This example is made up to show the steps. The text and measurements are hypothetical, not a customer order.

Say the text is RIVERSIDE, which has nine letters. The spot is shorter than 8 inches on its long side but longer than 6 inches, its short side has room to spare, and the background is a plain solid colour.

Step 1, letter count. Nine letters rules out 2x4 and 4x8, because both stop at 8. That leaves 2x6 (12 letters), 2x8 (16) and 3x8 (12).

Step 2, space. The long side is under 8 inches, so all three sizes with an 8-inch side are out. Only 2x6 is left. Its 6-inch side fits the spot with a little to spare.

Step 3, finish. The background is plain, so a mirror surface has a clean backdrop to reflect against. Matte is still the cheaper choice if price matters more than shine.

Step 4, price. The 2x6 starts at $59.95. Before ordering, the buyer checks the live price for 2x6 in the finish they chose.

Now change one thing. If the long side had been 8 inches or more, 2x8 and 3x8 would both have stayed in, and the short side of the spot would decide between them. A 3x8 fills more of a deep spot, and a 2x8 leaves room around it.

Have your letter count and measurements to hand, then set your own size and finish and see the price.

What to confirm before you order

The collection has one product, Custom Emblem Letter 3D Edition, and you set it up with two choices: size (five options) and surface (two options). The sections above cover both. A few things a buyer will want to know aren't covered here, so check them on the product page or ask the shop before ordering:

  • Material and how it attaches. This page doesn't state either one. Check the product page, or ask the shop, especially if your surface is curved or textured.
  • Indoor, outdoor or vehicle use. This page doesn't cover it either. If the emblem will face sun, rain or a car wash, confirm with the shop that it's made for that.
  • Font and colour choices. Check what the product page offers.
  • Proof before production. Ask whether you'll see a preview before the emblem is made.
  • Production and delivery time. Check at checkout or ask the shop.

How to apply it: before checkout, write your exact text, letter count, size and finish on one line. Then compare that line with what the order page shows back to you. Custom lettering goes wrong in two common ways, a typo or a count over the limit, and this one-line check catches both.

What to check

  • The exact spelling and capitalisation of your text.
  • Your letter count against the size's maximum.
  • That the finish in your cart is the one you meant.

When your line checks out, order your emblem with the text, size and finish you've settled on.
